segments.text: TinyStart is a calm focus app for getting started without guilt. Here's a fresh day.
I'll quick-capture one task: Draft project README.
A motivation note keeps the why visible — ship the course assignment on time.
Three tiny steps make starting easier: open outline, write setup, add the demo link.
Home shows the best next task — step one of three.
One tap to focus. I'll try a two-minute block.
Current step only, calm timer. Done with this step — we're moving.
Even a short focused block counts.
Session complete — affirming copy, no guilt metrics.
Today's focused minutes show up right on Home.
Daily recap reflects what helped. I'll tag Breakdown.
I built TinyStart using Specification-Driven Development. Every slice maps to IDs in requirements.md, and AGENTS.md tells the agent which spec wins.
I decided scope and tone: MVP only, shame-free copy, one primary CTA per screen. The agent implemented nine OpenSpec capabilities in order from openspec-capabilities.md.
Loop engineering in Cursor: one capability per session. Each change kept NFR-DX-01 green — lint, typecheck, vitest, and next build.
Maker not checker: review against verification.md, Playwright UI validation, and CodeRabbit on the pull request. This demo was generated entirely by agents.
